 1 Task Description
 The interactive Result Viewer and the corresponding CADINP module RESULTS are post- processing tools for the finite element modules of SOFiSTiK with a CDBASE database (e.g. ASE, TALPA, MAXIMA, BEMESS, AQB, DYNA, HASE or HYDRA). The programs allow the graphical, tabular and diagram-representation of Information and Results saved in the Database. The data is roughly structured/ grouped as follows:
 • System
 - Cross-Sections and cross-sectional values
 - Groups
 - Loadcaseinformation
 - Structural Elements
 - Nodes
 - Finite Elements (BEAM,QUAD,BRIC..)
 • Results
 - Stresses on cross-sections
 - Group results
 - Loadcase results (e.g. Sum of support forces)
 - Nodal results (Displacements, Rotations..)
 - Element results
 • Design
 - Element results(utilisation, stresses, required reinforcement..)
 The Representaion depends on the type of result and can be selected as:
 • Graphical representation (Text, Vector..)
 • Table
 • Diagram
 The resulting Document consists of:
 • Page
 - Graphic
 2 Layer
 Hint
 With version 2014 Result Viewer resp. RESULTS do replace the modules AQUP and DBView for cross-sectional and tabular post-processing. For the graphical result repre- sentation WinGRAF resp. WING are used.

From version 2022 we have moved a large part of the content to the new SOFiSTiK FEA manual.
 The new SOFiSTiK FEA Manual can be opened by following:
 https://www.sofistik.de/documentation/2025/en/fea/result_viewer/index_result_viewer.html
 Or you may also open the manual by following:
 Help Ribbon (SSD, Teddy, ...) → Online Help → FEA Manual
The modul results.exe has to be used for the batch start of Result Viewer via console. This modul is used automatically if it is running within the program WPS or SPS.
The input is done in a free format with the CADINP input language (see the general manual SOFiSTiK: ’Basics’).

The input table shown is a structured specification for the “Result Viewer” module of a SOFiSTiK-related workflow (FEA/structural). It is organized as a sequence of record types (keyword rows) that are processed only within a single input block terminated by an `END` marker. Within that block, records are evaluated in order, but there is a key distinction between **attribute records** and **demand records**:

- **Attribute records**: Most records in the block fall into this category. Their values are updated immediately, i.e., they affect the internal state for subsequent outputs.
- **Demand records**: These records trigger the actual creation of output lists/tables/plots (in the next rendering step). In particular, demand records named explicitly (or implied by keywords) include:
  - `STRU`: structural elements representation (system values, input items, numbering, designations shown as a table)
  - `CROS`: cross-section representation, including cross-section values and stress/results on cross-sections
  - `NODE`: node results representation (displacements, support reactions, boundary forces as a table)
  - `QUAD`: scalar/vector/tensor variables for quadrilateral elements shown as a list (examples: moment, shear/flow, principal stresses or reinforcement)
  - `BEAM`: line representation for frame/girder systems (e.g., bending moments) as a table
  - `BRIC`: results at volume elements as a table

There is also logic affecting demand records: if in a demand record the literal `DSGN` is given for `TYPE`, **only attributes are set**, and the output effect is deferred/avoided for that demand. This means the record can be used to configure context without generating a result entity.

## Record/keyword inventory visible in the table
The table lists many keyword fields that act as attributes or configuration parameters. Several appear multiple times, indicating grouped configurations per output context (e.g., repeated blocks for different demand types):

- General flow/control and formatting attributes (as named entries in the table text):  
  `HEAD`, `END`, `PAGE` (not detailed here; referenced as per general manual), plus `TICK`, `LABL`, `DLABL` (tick labels / label behavior), `MODE`, `REPR` (representation mode), `FILL` (fill style), `UNIT` (unit scaling), `SCHH` (likely section/height or style-related numeric parameter).
- Structural and data scope attributes:  
  `STRU`, `TYPE`, `ETYP`, `REPR`, `FILL`, `UNIT`, `SCHH` appear as a grouped set under a structural context.
- Cross-section related attributes:  
  `CROS`, `TYPE`, `ETYP`, `STYP`, `REPR`, `FILL`, `UNIT`, `SCHH` appear as another grouped set for cross-section outputs.
- Additional configuration fields shown as tokens/keywords (standalone list in the excerpt):  
  `ALIG`, `VAL`, `DESC`, `DIAX`, `AXIS`, `MODE`, `TICK`, `LABL`, `DLABL`, `STRU`, `TYPE`, `ETYP`, `REPR`, `FILL`, `UNIT`, `SCHH`, `CROS`, `TYPE`, `ETYP`, `STYP`, `REPR`, `FILL`, `UNIT`, `SCHH`.

## Semantics of output production
The excerpt further states rendering rules relevant to interpreting the table:
- Tables and plots are produced on **`BRIC`** (a key output target), implying that despite multiple demand records existing, the tabular/graphical finalization may occur via `BRIC`.
- “The other input records” (i.e., non-demand/attribute records) are used to configure behavior rather than to directly trigger output generation.
- “Tables are partly combined, if no sequence of the records is free” indicates that when multiple demand/attribute records are present, some outputs may be merged depending on record ordering and availability of free sequences.
- The “dimension of the results is determined … with the input `DBO`” indicates a global or external parameter affecting how numeric results are scaled/expressed.

Overall, this table is essentially a **configuration schema** for selecting what results to display (structure, cross-sections, nodes, quads, beams, volumes) and how to present them (units, representation, labels, axes, styling).

The table shown is a **record/item specification** for Result Viewer style input, listing the supported *records* (first column) and, for each record, the allowed **items/keywords** (second column). In the surrounding context, each input block is processed sequentially: **attribute records** primarily update settings immediately, while their visual/numerical effects appear only in the *next* list or drawing. **Demand records** request specific outputs (e.g., STRU, CROS, NODE, QUAD, BEAM, BRIC). This table focuses on the **attribute/control records** and their parameters.

## Structure of the table
- **Column 1 (“Record”)**: identifies the record type (e.g., CDB, SIZE, PI CT AND FF).
- **Column 2 (“Items”)**: enumerates the keywords/parameters that belong to that record. Some records group several parameters on the same line; line breaks in the table reflect additional items belonging to the same record.

## Record groups and their items

### 1) CDB / SIZE / PICT AND / FF
- **CDB**: items **NO**, **TITLE** – likely selects a database/configuration block number and a human-readable title.
- **SIZE**: items define overall scaling and formatting:
  - **TYPE**, **SC**, **W**, **H**, **MARG**, **FORM**, **SPLl**
  - Secondary sizing/scalar controls: **SCAL**, **HLEG**, **WLEG**, **SLEG**, **LEGW**, **FREE**, **UMBR**
  - Additional options: **SHAE**, **DATE**, **ASB**, **ARCH**, **DRUL**, **DRUR**, **DRUD**
- **PICT AND**: items **M**, **W**, **H**, **MSCA**, **TITL**, **SPLT** – picture sizing and title/splitting behavior for the graphic output.
- **FF**: item list ends the PICT/FF block (used as a formatting terminator or page/file part indicator depending on the system conventions).

### 2) GRP / VIEW
- **GRP**: items **NUMB**, **OPTI**, **ETYP** – defines a grouping of display components; **ETYP** suggests element type or entity type context.
- **VIEW**:
  - items **TYPE**, **X**, **Y**, **Z**, **ACHS**
  - indicates a viewing/camera configuration with coordinates and an axis selection (**ACHS**).

### 3) LC / DBO / FLT / FILT / JOIN / XLSX / TINF
This section contains extensive filtering and layout options.
- **LC**: items **NO**, **T**, **DESI**, **MAT**, **REF**, **NMAT**, **CS**, plus **XI**, **XIV**, **ENO**, **X**, **SECT**, **TITL**
  - Additional properties: **NAME**, **OPTI**, **UNIT**, **ND**, **POS**, **WIDT**, **SORT**
  - plus repeat formatting fields: **REPE**, **FORM**, **BMIN**, **BMAX**, **TITL**
- **DBO / DBO…**: includes items **NAME**, **OPTI**, **UNIT**, **ND**, **POS**, **WIDT**, **SORT**, and **REPE/FORM/BMIN/BMAX/TITL** as part of data selection and annotation.
- **FLT** / **FILT**: filtering parameterization:
  - **FLT**: **ID**, **NAME**, **RULE**, **ACT**
  - **FILT**: **NAME**, **TYPE**, **OPTI**, **VAL1**, **VAL2**, **EXRF**
- **JOIN**: **COL1**, **COL2** – column join/merge behavior.
- **XLSX**: items **NAME**, **WS**, **ROW**, **COL**, **CLNM**, **TIME**, **CDB**, plus **ELEM**, **FILT**, **RESU**
  - suggests exporting/importing from XLSX-like sources for element result tables.
- **TINF**: items **TYPE**, **MEDI**, **OPTI** – additional table-information controls (e.g., mediation/aggregation and option flags).

### 4) PFA / PLN / PMR / TXTP
These records define plotting/labeling behavior and parameter mapping.
- **PFA**: items **ID1**, **ID2**, **ID3**, **ID4**, **COLO**, **R**, **G** – color/parameter assignments (R/G channels and a **COLO** mapping).
- **PLN**: similar structure: **ID1–ID4**, **COLO**, **R**, **G**.
- **PMR**: **ID1–ID4**, **COLO**, **R**, **G**.
- **TXTP**: items **SHOW**, **OVLP** – text visibility and overlap handling.

### 5) DIAG / D GRA (partial)
The bottom portion starts additional display/annotation records:
- **DIAG**: items **X**, **Y**, **GDEF**, **LCTP**, **YUP**, **LEGE**, **LBAX**, plus **SPPL**, **AXFU**
  - indicates diagnostic/diagram settings: coordinate anchors, legend, axes labeling, and scaling/appearance.
- **DGRA**: items **DESC**, **VAL1**, **VAL2** – likely description/graph annotation with two value parameters.

## Relationship to demand records (from the context)
While demand records (e.g., **STRU, CROS, NODE, QUAD, BEAM, BRIC**) request the actual output content, the records listed here mainly configure **how** that content is displayed: sizing, view/camera, grouping, data selection (LC/DBO), filtering (FLT/FILT), data sources (XLSX), color/text/legend behavior (PFA/PLN/PMR/TXTP/DIAG), and diagram/graph descriptors (DGRA). Per the provided context, these attribute settings take effect on the **next** list/drawing command (i.e., the subsequent demand record).

### Table Description (RAG-Friendly)

This table belongs to the SOFiSTiK **Result Viewer** input format. The input is processed **block-wise**: the viewer consumes a single input block that ends with **`END`**. Within the block, records are analyzed **in order**, and most records are **attribute records** that update internal settings immediately. However, these settings typically become **visible only in the next list or drawing** that is generated after the attribute updates.  

A key distinction is that the table may contain both **attribute records** (configuration/control) and **demand records** (explicitly requesting a representation of results). In particular, if the literal **`DSGN`** is given for **`TYPE`** in a demand record, then **only attributes are set** and **no new result output** is produced.

#### Demand records (result outputs)
The input block contains (or can contain) demand records that request different output types. In this case, the system indicates the following possible demand records, which each correspond to a specific result visualization/export mode:

- **`STRU`**: Representation of **structural elements**. Includes system values, input items, numbering, and designations, presented as a table.
- **`CROS`**: Representation of **cross sections** and associated values/results on cross sections (e.g., stresses) presented as a table.
- **`NODE`**: Representation of **results at nodes**, such as displacements, support reactions, boundary forces, as a table.
- **`QUAD`**: Representation for **quadrilateral elements**. A scalar, vector, or tensor variable (e.g., moment, shear force/flow, principal stresses or reinforcements) is provided as a **list**.
- **`BEAM`**: Line representation for **frame/girder** systems, such as bending moments, presented as a table.
- **`BRIC`**: Representation at **volume elements**, as a table.

Additionally, the table shows several attribute-like records relevant to formatting/styling and selection (see below).

#### Attribute/configuration records (applied to subsequent outputs)
The table includes multiple configuration records that control formatting, labeling, modes, and layout. The repeated presence of groups (e.g., `CROS` appears more than once) suggests that the attribute settings can be redefined before subsequent demand outputs.

The following fields/records are listed as part of the input schema and/or attribute controls:

- **General interface/formatting**: `D L I N`, `ALIG`, `VAL`, `DESC`, `DIAX`, `AXIS`
- **Model selection/mode**: `MODE`
- **Tick/label formatting**: `TICK`, `LABL`, `DLAB`
- **Structured output selection blocks**: `STRU`, `TYPE`, `ETYP`, `REPR`, `FILL`, `UNIT`, `SCHH`
- **Cross-section output blocks** (again): `CROS`, `TYPE`, `ETYP`, `STYP`, `REPR`, `FILL`, `UNIT`, `SCHH`

These attribute records define how the subsequent output requested by the demand record will be constructed (e.g., which type/element category, how results are represented, how regions are filled, which unit system is used, and how shading/scale height is set via `SCHH`).

#### Metadata records
The documentation note states that **`HEAD`**, **`PAGE`**, and **`END`** are part of the general manual and correspond to header/page handling and block termination.

**In summary:** this table section defines the **control-and-demand structure** of a Result Viewer block. Most records act as **attributes** that configure formatting and representation for upcoming output, while demand records (`STRU`, `CROS`, `NODE`, `QUAD`, `BEAM`, `BRIC`) trigger actual result visualization as tables or lists depending on element/result type.

The table is a compact specification of **Result Viewer output records** that define what kind of results are rendered and which formatting/legend parameters apply. It belongs to an input block that processes records sequentially: most rows are **attribute records** that update internal settings immediately, while their visual effect becomes visible only when a subsequent demand/list/drawing record is handled. If a demand record sets `TYPE` to the literal `DSGN`, only attributes are set (no actual demand-driven results are generated).

Each row in the table corresponds to one **demand record type** (i.e., a result category). The **first column** gives the record name; the **second column** lists the “Items” (fields/attributes) that can be specified for that record. The table therefore documents the expected item keys for configuring each output.

### Record: NODE
`NODE` is used to represent **results in nodes** (e.g., displacements, support reactions, boundary forces as a table). The table lists these item keys:
- `TYPE` (result selection/category for node results)
- `TOTA` (total/aggregation option or totality flag)
- `REPR` (how values are represented, e.g., numeric formatting/style)
- `FILL` (visual filling style/legend behavior)
- `UNIT` (display unit)
- `UNI2` (secondary/alternative unit label or unit conversion output)
- `SCHH` (scale/height/size parameter, typically affecting visualization sizing)

### Record: BEAM
`BEAM` specifies results for **line representations** in frame/girder systems (e.g., bending moments as a table/diagram).
Item keys:
- `TYPE` (what beam result to display)
- `STYP` (subtype/style of result, e.g., component or variant)
- `REPR` (representation mode)
- `FILL` (fill style)
- `UNIT` (unit)
- `SCHH` (size/scale/spacing related parameter)

### Record: QUAD
`QUAD` defines scalar/vector/tensor results for **quadrilateral elements** (e.g., moment, shear force/flow, principal stresses, reinforcement) often as a list.
Item keys are split across two lines in the table:
- First part: `TYPE`, `STYP`, `TOTA`, `AVER`, `REPR`, `FILL`, `UNIT`
- Second part: `SCHH`
Thus, `QUAD` includes both aggregation/statistics controls (`TOTA`, `AVER`) and rendering controls (`REPR`, `FILL`, `SCHH`) plus unit control.

### Record: BRIC
`BRIC` specifies results at **volume (brick) elements** as a table.
Item keys:
- `TYPE`, `STYP`, `TOTA`, `AVER`, `REPR`, `FILL`, `UNIT`
- plus `SCHH` (size/scale/visual parameter)

### Overall meaning
Across all four records, the recurring items indicate a consistent schema:
- **Result selection:** `TYPE` (and `STYP` for BEAM/QUAD/BRIC)
- **Aggregation/statistics:** `TOTA`, `AVER`
- **Visualization/formatting:** `REPR`, `FILL`, `SCHH`
- **Units:** `UNIT` and, specifically for `NODE`, `UNI2`

This table therefore acts as a schema reference: it tells which configuration fields are available for each demand record category used by the Result Viewer.

Result Viewer processes only a single input block which is finished with END. The input is analysed in turn within this input block. In this case one must distinguish between attributes and demand records. Most of the input records are attribute records. The values of this records are updated immediatly. However, their effects become visible only in the next list or drawing. If the literal DSGN is given for TYPE in the demand records, only the attributes are set. Currently there are following demand records:
 STRU Representation of structural elements. System values, input items, numbering as well as designations will represented as table.
 CROS Representation of cross section and cross section values and results (stresses) on cross sections.
 NODE Representation of results in nodes (e.g. displacements, support reactions and boundary forces) as table.
 QUAD Representation of a scalar variable (e.g. moment), vector (e.g. shear force or flow) or tensor (e.g. principal stresses or reinforcements) for quadrilateral elements as list.
 BEAM Representation of a line representation for frame and girder systems (e.g. bending moments) as table.
 BRIC Representation of results at volume elements as table.

 The records HEAD, END and PAGE are described in the general manual SOFiSTiK: ’FEA / STRUCTURAL Installation and Basics’.
 The description of the various records follow.

The table describes configuration fields used for selecting/opening an input database within a CDB (current database) workflow. It is focused specifically on how to reference an external or previously defined database when importing an input .CDB/.results file.

**Table structure and columns**
- **Item**: Identifier for each configuration entry (e.g., “NO”, “TITI”).
- **Description**: Human-readable explanation of what the field controls.
- **Unit**: Indicates the expected data unit/type for the field. In this table, units are either “–” (no unit) or “LIT” (used as a placeholder type/format).
- **Default**: The default value applied when the parameter is not explicitly set.

**Row 1 (Item: NO)**
- **Meaning**: “Reference number of the database.”
- **Behavior**:
  - The field is used to refer to which database should be used during the start of the input process.
  - **Value 0** is special: it instructs the system to **use the current database** during the start of input.
  - This aligns with the surrounding context: *the current database is closed and a new input database is opened*, but when the database was previously defined with a TITL, only the **reference number** is required to identify it.
- **Unit**: “–” (no measurement unit).
- **Default**: **1**, meaning the system initially assumes database reference number 1 unless changed.

**Row 2 (Item: TITL)**
- **Meaning**: “Path and name of the database.”
- **Role**:
  - Provides the **filesystem path and name** of the database.
  - The default is **\***, indicating that the field is typically not a fixed path by default; rather, it may act as a wildcard or placeholder resolved in context.
- **Unit**: “LIT” (likely indicating a literal/text input type).
- **Default**: **\***.

**Operational context (from additional text)**
- When switching databases for graphical outputs, the selection of the input database for graphics/lists/diagrams **cannot be changed via the user interface** after opening a .results file containing such an input; the selection becomes disabled.  
- Consequently, the table’s fields primarily govern which database is opened/selected programmatically, while UI-based switching may be restricted.

Overall, the table defines the minimal parameters needed to either (a) reference an already-defined database using its reference number (**NO**), or (b) define the database location/name when needed (**TITL**), with explicit behavior for **NO = 0** to keep using the current database at input start.

CDB
 The current database is closed and the new input database is opened with the input CDB. Only the reference number of the database has to be given in the case of previous definition of this database with TITL.

This table documents the configurable parameters that control the *output paper/layout size and border rendering* for a drawing/plot in the SOFiSTiIK plotting/report system. It is structured as columns **Item** (parameter name), **Description** (meaning and allowed values), **Unit** (measurement unit when applicable), and **Default** (system default).

### Parameters and meanings
**TYPE (Paper size)**  
- Selects the paper format. The table notes two orientation conventions using the sign of the value:  
  - **Positive** → **landscape** format  
  - **Negative** → **portrait** format  
- The unit is shown as “–/LIT” and the **default is `WIN`**, meaning the format of the currently defined Windows printer is used (or Windows’ default printer if not set interactively).

**SC (Scale)**  
- Controls drawing scale. The unit is “–” (scale is numeric but not labeled by physical unit). Default is “-” (no fixed default shown).  
- **SC = 0** has a special meaning: the program uses the **largest possible drawing** (i.e., ignores conservative scale reduction and fills the page as much as feasible).  
- **SC = –** (other values) include engineering-scale behavior: the program can apply **best-possible filling** using engineering scales such as **1:1, 1:2, 1:5, …**  
- **\*1.E+10** is mentioned as a special marker to “use this scale” (i.e., force a particular scale interpretation).

**W (Paper width)**  
- Width of the paper canvas area. Unit: **cm**.  
- Default is “-” (not fixed; behavior depends on TYPE and SC logic).

**H (Paper height)**  
- Height of the paper canvas area. Unit: **cm**.  
- Default is “-”.

### Border and margin options
**MARG (Draws a border)**  
- A switch controlling whether borders/margins are drawn around the plotting area. Unit: **LIT**. Default: **`FULL`**.  
- Allowed values:  
  - **OFF**: no border.  
  - **NO**: draws an **inner border** and places the **scale** “here”; **W and H define the area to be drawn** (notably for single-sheet plotters and laser printers).  
  - **YES**: considers a **free border margin** around the drawing using **W and H with a 2 cm margin** (otherwise 5 cm is mentioned).  
  - **FULL**: draws an **additional outer border** intended for cutting the drawing at the **outer paper limits**, typically for **drum plotters**.

**FORM (Form of the border)**  
- Selects the border frame style. Unit: **LIT**. Default: `*` (asterisk indicates a variable/default not concretely specified in the snippet).  
- Values shown:  
  - **STAN**: standard frame  
  - **ZTVK**: ZTVK-88 frame (title-band/report-style frame)  
  - **URS**: Report Browser definition

The table segment describes the parameter **“SIZE”** used to determine the **paper format and layout geometry** for generated drawings (e.g., report browser documents, printed plots, pictures). It explains that paper size can be defined in **two main ways**, and then lists supported **format codes/options** (including DIN, ANSI, and Hewlett-Packard plotter sizes), plus related layout controls for margins, legends, and title bands.

## 1) Two variations to define paper size
1. **Implicit format selection via `TYPE`** (or explicit via `W` and `H`):
   - The user selects a paper format using `TYPE`, or specifies **width `W`** and **height `H`**.
   - If scale is not explicitly given, the program selects a scale automatically, choosing the **largest possible scale** while considering engineering scale preferences (examples: **1:1, 1:2, 1:5**, etc.).
   - If an explicit scale parameter **`SC`** is feasible, it is used.
   - Setting **`SC = 0`** forces the program to use the **largest possible drawing**, effectively overriding scale limits to maximize size.

2. **User-specified scale with automatic paper size selection**:
   - The user specifies scale; by setting **either `W` or `H` to zero**, the system automatically chooses the corresponding paper size that fits the other dimension and the scale.
   - If only one of `W`/`H` is zero, the scale definition can be inferred/dropped because it becomes defined by the remaining dimension.

## 2) `TYPE` option values and meanings (including orientation)
The table lists allowed `TYPE` codes to select paper sizes and printer formats:
- **`URS`**: Default Report Browser document format.
- **`WIN`**: Current Windows printer format (defined in the last interactive session); otherwise uses the Windows default printer.
- **ANSI sizes**: `A`, `B`, `C`, `D` with dimensions given in inches (A: 11×8.5, B: 17×11, C: 22×17, D: 34×22).
- **Hewlett-Packard plotter papers**: `HPA`, `HPB`, `HPC`, `HPD`, `HP4`, `HP3`, `HP2`, `HP1` with dimensions given in mm (multiple HP variants listed).
- There are also entries for **Matrix/Laser printers**:
  - **Matrix printer**: **8×12 inch** (200×287 mm) for `MP,-MP` and **wider matrix** `MPW` / `LP,-LP` context (14×12 inch mentioned).
  - **Laser printer**: A4 option described as **198.4×280 mm**.
- **Orientation control**: A leading **minus sign** before the `TYPE` code selects **portrait orientation** (as indicated for “preceeding minus sign selects the portrait orientation”).

## 3) Framing behavior for pictures
- **Pictures are generated without frame** in this step; the **frame is added later** in the “Result Browser”.

## 4) Margin and legend/title layout parameters
Beyond paper size, the table continues with layout-related sizing:
- **Right margin definition**: controlled by **`WLEG`**, “usually available only as margin”.
- **Bottom border height**: typically **1.0 cm**, used to place designation with **`HEAD` lines**.
- **Legend line limits**: only limited HEAD lines are expected in combined result drawings; more lines may be possible if **enlarged legends** are defined via **`HLEG`** (headline) or **`SLEG`** (picture legend).
- **Placement of designation**: controlled by **`HLEG`** sign:
  - **`HLEG < 0`**: designation at **left-hand side**.
  - **`HLEG > 0`**: designation at **right-hand side**, requiring smaller text; preferred for readability on folded plans when drawings are larger than **TYPE 4**.

## 5) Title bands and axis placement (ZTVK and layout rules)
- **`ZTVK`**: produces a drawing title in **DIN A4 portrait**, including **upper and lower title bands**.
- The **title band sizes** can be defined by **`HLEG`**.
- The program references how specific **HEAD lines** map to printed bands:
  - The first **HEAD line** prints on the structure line.
  - Subsequent **RESULTS HEAD lines** map to structure descriptions such as building part line, bar line, event line.
- For formats with **heights from 27 to 30 cm**, the **plot is positioned between the bands**.
- In **larger formats**, the bands appear as **drawing title at the right side** of the plot.
- **Coordinate axes**, reduction scale factors, result designations, and a **1 cm sample line** are placed **except for header/title lines**, i.e., they occupy the plot area between/around the bands.

The table describes configuration parameters related to plotting “SIZE” and the surrounding layout areas for a report/picture generation system (e.g., SOFiMSHA/C / Result Browser). It lists each **Item** (parameter name), a **Description** of what it controls, the **Unit** (data type/measurement), and a **Default** value.

**SPLI** controls how the paper is partitioned into multiple picture tiles. The description specifies two possible interpretations:  
- `height × width create pictures column by column`  
- `height × width create pictures line by line`  
Its default is **`1*1`**, meaning the paper is not tiled (single picture).

**SCAL** defines which dimensional (coordinate) lines are drawn. It accepts values:
- `-` : draws coordinates  
- `YZ` : Y and Z coordinates  
- `ZX` : Z and X coordinates  
- `XY` : X and Y coordinates  
The unit is **LIT** (a literal/enum-like option), and its default is **`-`** (draw coordinates).

**HLEG** is a field reserved for the legend under the plot. Unit is **cm**, default **`1.0`**. This effectively sets vertical space used for the legend area beneath the plotted content (including limited legend lines as noted in the context text).

**WLEG** reserves a field for an own legend to the right of the plot. Unit **cm**, default **`0.0`**, meaning right legend is not used unless explicitly set. In the additional text, it is also clarified that the “size of the right margin” can be defined by **WLEG**, typically for margin/legend purposes.

**SLEG** sets the height of the partial legend (unit **cm**, default **`2.0`**). This parameter influences how many legend entries fit vertically and interacts with limitations mentioned for legend lines.

**LEGW** is the width of the legend if it is placed in the picture. Unit **cm**, default **`*`** (unspecified/automatic). A `*` default implies the program chooses an appropriate width based on other layout constraints.

**FREE** defines a region to be released around the structure (i.e., additional whitespace/margin around the main drawing). Unit **cm**, default `*` (automatic). This affects available plot area and thus how titles/bands and legends can fit.

**UMBR** controls “line feed” behavior in the picture legend (unit **LIT**). Default **`YES`**. Supported modes (from the table and description):  
- `NO` : no line wrapping/feeding  
- `YES` : wrap/feeed if a line is too long  
- `SUPP` : shorten a long line by removing characters at the next blank  
- `SHOR` : shorten also within a word

Overall, this table specifies fine-grained control over **tiling (SPLI)**, **coordinate/measurement line selection (SCAL)**, and **legend/title/margin geometry** via **HLEG, WLEG, SLEG, LEGW, FREE**, and **legend text formatting** via **UMBR**. The accompanying context text further explains that larger formats adjust legend/title placement, right-side placement may require smaller text, picture frames are handled separately, and header/title bands interact with available plot height.

The provided table content is a structured “AND / input combination” specification used for generating and ordering drawing results (graphics). It is accompanied by field headers shown as “Item Description Unit Default” and references to related tables/parameters: **SIZE, PICT, FF**.

### Purpose and semantics
This table describes how the system should combine and lay out multiple result records when the input expression uses the logical operator **AND**. The key rule is that lists are combined **“as far as possible”**: when the sequence contains result types from the set **STR, CROS, NODE, BEAM, QUAD, BRIC**, the system tries to merge them into fewer output lists unless other records intervene.

An example is given to clarify how the internal grouping works:
- Input: `NODE UZ REPR DLST; QUAD MX STYP ELEM; NODE SZ; QUAD N STYP ELEM`
- Output behavior: this produces **two lists**—the first list contains **NODE** results and the second list contains **QUAD** results.  
This implies that, although adjacent or compatible result specifications are merged, **different entity categories (NODE vs QUAD)** may remain in separate lists when they are not naturally merged into one continuous list.

### “AND” behavior (table consolidation)
The table further defines that an input expression containing **AND** merges those previously separate results into **one combined table**:
- “An input of **AND** also combines the two results into one table.”

In other words:
- Without AND: results may remain split across multiple lists (e.g., NODE list vs QUAD list).
- With AND: the system consolidates those lists into a single unified table (one output structure).

### Graphics / pagination implications
The table also includes rendering rules:
- If **AND is not given**, a **new drawing is created**.
- If **AND is given**, the input represents the **next drawing order (layer) within the same picture**, and the **scale remains unchanged**.

A separate pagination/formatting rule is included:
- To create a page break, the system uses **FF** or **SIZE** (“To create a page break the input FF or SIZE are given.”).  
This establishes that **FF/SIZE are page/format controls**, while **AND controls drawing layering vs new drawing creation**.

### Key referenced parameters
- **SIZE**: used to force a page break / pagination behavior.
- **PICT**: referenced as related context (likely picture/table output grouping).
- **FF**: explicitly stated as a page break trigger.

The visible header “Item Description Unit Default” indicates that this documentation is part of a parameter table where each configurable item would typically have:
- an identifier (“Item”),
- a meaning (“Description”),
- a measurement unit (“Unit”, when applicable),
- and an “Default” value if omitted.
However, the excerpt primarily specifies **behavioral rules** rather than enumerating actual item rows.

### Table: LC parameter selection and scope for load/design case representation

This table defines how the program selects **load cases (LC)** and related variants for use in subsequent result drawings/output. It contains columns **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**.

---

#### 1) **Item: NO**
- **Purpose:** Selects a **load case** number for representation in the following drawings.
- **Unit:** Listed as `–/LIT` (categorical/list value).
- **Default:** `DEFA`, i.e., **Default = FIRST**.
- **Interpretation rules for numeric NO:**
  - If **NO ≥ 0**: use the specified load case.
  - If **NO < 0**: use the load case whose number equals **the entry from the load case list** at position `|NO|` (i.e., negative values reference the list rather than directly selecting by number).
- **Named selection modes:**
  - `DEFA`: default selection (uses the first available load case from the list).
  - `FIRS`: uses the **first** load case from the load case list.
  - `LAST`: uses the **last** load case.
  - `NEXT`: uses the **next** load case.
  - `PREV`: uses the **previous** load case.
  - `All`: uses **all load cases**.
  - `NAME`: resolves the load case number via its **TITLE** (with a warning if not found exactly).
  - `FIND`: resolves like `NAME` but **without warning** (more tolerant matching).

- **List syntax / multiple selection in one list (important for RAG indexing):**
  - More than one load/design/history case (or cross-section) can be output in one list by writing multiple numbers **in a row**, e.g.:
    - `LC NO 1,2,3,4,5`
  - A generation form is also supported, e.g.:
    - `LC NO (1 5 1)` to represent a sequence (here conceptually from 1 to 5 with step 1).

**Contextual linkage to stored results (from provided notes):**  
The **input of a load case** affects how **all results stored relative to that load case** are represented. Results like **reinforcement/design stresses (BEMESS)** and **beam stresses (AQB)** are tied to the **design load case** input, while other load-case-wise stored results are addressed by **NO**. Beam section selection depends on **ENO and X**.

---

#### 2) **Item: T**
- **Purpose:** Selects a **time value for transient results**.
- **Unit:** `sec/LIT` (time in seconds, list value).
- **Default:** `LAST` (use the last time step).
- **Equivalence rule:** The input value (except `NAME` / `FIND`) is **equivalently treated as NO**, meaning numeric entries select by index/value consistent with the NO mechanism.

---

#### 3) **Item: DESI**
- **Purpose:** Selects a **design case** (e.g., reinforcement and design stresses).
- **Unit:** `–/LIT`.
- **Default:** `DEFA`.
- **Equivalence rule:** Input (except `NAME` / `FIND`) is treated equivalently to **NO**, i.e., it uses the same selection/index logic but for design cases rather than load cases.

**Contextual linkage to stored results (from provided notes):**  
With the input of the **design load case**, program-generated **reinforcement/design stresses** (BEMESS) and **beam stresses** (AQB) are represented accordingly; other load-case-wise results are addressed by **NO**.

---

Overall, this table specifies a compact but flexible selection interface: numeric selection (direct or list-based via sign), symbolic selectors (FIRS/LAST/NEXT/PREV), name-based lookup (NAME/FIND), and multi-item output using comma-separated lists or generation expressions.

content:
### Table Description (LC)

This table defines the **load case (LC)** selector used to determine **which results are referenced, stored, or activated** in the system. It primarily controls how output data (e.g., stresses and reinforcement-related results) are mapped to a given load/design/history context.

---

#### Key concept: Load-case dependent result representation
The input of an **LC** value affects the representation of **all results stored relative to that load case**. In other words, results are not merely labeled; their association with a specific LC influences how they are interpreted and presented.

---

#### Interaction with other result sources (reinforcements and stresses)
The table also clarifies that certain result types are tied directly to specialized “design” processing:

- **Reinforcements** and **design stresses from BEMESS**
- **Beam stresses from AQB**

These are **represented when the design load case is input**. Therefore, selecting the proper LC is necessary to ensure that reinforcement and design stress results correspond to the intended design scenario.

By contrast, **all other load-case-wise stored results** are addressed by **NO**. This implies a separation between:
- result sets that depend on a specific **design load case**, and
- general results stored per load case, selected through **NO**.

---

#### Beam section selection (ENO and X)
Results (e.g., stresses) are stored in **beam sections**. When **ENO** and **X** are provided, the system selects the **beam section corresponding to the current load case**. Thus, LC determines the load/design context, while ENO and X determine *where* within the beam the results are extracted.

---

#### Special note: unused items
The table explicitly states that the items **T, MAT, REF, NMAT, and CS** are **not used yet**. This indicates that, although the table schema may contain these fields, they currently do not influence behavior or result selection.

---

#### Selecting multiple load/design/history cases
A single output list can contain **more than one load/design/history case or cross section**, using a format that writes multiple numbers **in a row**. For example:

- To include load cases **1 through 5** in the same list:
  - `LC NO 1,2,3,4,5`
- Or via a generation instruction:
  - `LC NO (1 5 1)`

This means the LC table supports both **explicit enumeration** and **range-based expansion** to generate multiple references in one output command.

The table documents input options for result representation, specifically how results are selected and interpreted for different material references and thickness/depth locations. It is structured as rows (“Item”, “Description”, “Unit”, “Default”) and lists configurable keywords used to control which data—such as material-dependent values, nonlinear material laws, or quad-layer stresses—are taken from stored analysis results.

The “MAT” row defines the selection of the material to be represented, particularly for composite materials. The unit column shows “/–LIT”, and the default is “DEFA”. The description clarifies that the MAT input (except for the “NAME / FIND” mechanism) behaves equivalently to selecting by “NO”. Additionally, MAT can be used to input the literal of a stress point from program AQUA for beam output. The selection can be directed to representative statistic functions from a material list: average (“_MID”), maximum (“_MAX”), minimum (“_MIN”), absolute maximum (“_AMX”), absolute minimum (“_AMN”), and last value (“_LST”).

The “REF” row specifies a reference material used in addition to MAT. Its unit is “–” and default is “-”, meaning it is optional/neutral unless provided. Conceptually, REF allows one to augment or reference another material context beyond the primary MAT choice.

The “NMAT” row covers nonlinear result cases where the material law itself must be selected (e.g., nonlinear results from TALPA/ASE). Its unit is “/–LIT”, and default is “STAN”. The description states that N MAT is equivalent to MAT in selection semantics, but specifically targets the law for nonlinear computations.

The “CS” row introduces “Construction stage” as a selection criterion. It has unit “–” and default “0”, indicating no stage offset unless explicitly set.

Two related depth-selection rows follow for quad-type stress representations: “XI” and “XIV”. “XI” is used to select the depth (e.g., a QUAD layer stress). Its unit is “LIT” and default “FAC”. The description defines allowed symbolic options mapping to depth locations based on element thickness: “FAC” uses XIV as a factor of element thickness (from upper side -1 to lower side +1), while “TH” uses XIV in meters from the lower side upward. “THD” uses XIV in meters from the upper side downward. “TM” uses XIV in meters from the middle downward (“middle” reference), “TMU” uses XIV from the middle upward, and “ALL” indicates all layers. These options control how XIV is interpreted physically.

Finally, the “XIV” row specifies “Layer depth” with unit “–/m” and default “0.0”. This value is then interpreted according to how “XI” was chosen (factor-based or meter-from-boundary based).

Additional context included with the table (relevant for how results are stored) explains that certain load-case items (T, MAT, REF, NMAT, CS) are “not used yet”, while the load case input affects representation of all stored results relative to that load case. It also clarifies the difference between reinforcement/design stresses from external programs (represented when design load cases are selected) and other load-case-wise stored results (addressed by NO). It further explains how multiple load/design/history cases and cross sections can be listed in one output via REPR DLST, using either comma-separated rows or generation syntax (e.g., LC NO (1 5 1)).

The table describes the meaning and usage of the parameter **LC** in a structural/numerical results management context (likely a system that stores and retrieves results per load case and/or design case). It clarifies how load-case inputs affect the way stored results are represented, and how selection of particular results is performed for beam sections and reinforcement/design outputs.

### Key elements and their roles
- **LC (Load Case / Load-Case Identifier)**: Acts as the controlling identifier that determines which set of results are associated with the given load case. The table explicitly notes that **the input of a load case (or design load case)** has a global effect on how **all results referenced to that load case** are represented.
- The table states that the items **T, MAT, REF, NMAT and CS are not used yet**. This suggests that, in this part of the system, those fields are either placeholders, not currently implemented, or not relevant for the LC selection logic.

### How results are categorized and selected
- **Reinforcements**, **design stresses from BEMESS**, and **beam stresses from AQB** are **represented when a design load case** is provided. In other words, some result types are tied specifically to design-oriented processing rather than to ordinary load case processing.
- **All other load case–wise stored results** are addressed by **NO**. This indicates a two-level structure:
  1. **LC** selects the load/design case context for representation.
  2. **NO** selects which stored result set (for non-design load-case-wise results) is targeted within that context.

### Beam section selection mechanism
- Results (e.g., stresses) are stored **in beam sections**. The table specifies that, **with the input of ENO and X**, the **beam section of the current load case** is selected.
  - Here, **ENO** and **X** together define which section’s results should be read or displayed for the given LC context.

### Multi-selection capability (REPR DLST)
The table explains that it is possible to output **more than one load/design/history case or cross section in one list**, using **REPR DLST**. To enable this:
- Multiple numbers must be written **in a row**, separated as part of a single list entry.
- Example: using load cases **1 through 5** in the same list:  
  **LC NO 1,2,3,4,5**
- Example using a generation instruction (range syntax):  
  **LC NO (1 5 1)**  
  which indicates a sequence from 1 to 5 with step size 1.

### Summary of table intent
Overall, the table defines **LC** as a master selector affecting the representation of all results tied to a load/design case, while delineating that:
- design-related outputs are tied to **design load case input**, and
- most other results rely on **NO** for load-case-wise selection,
- with additional controls (**ENO, X**) for beam section result retrieval,
- and support for multi-case list output via **REPR DLST** using explicit enumeration or range generation.

The table defines the **LC (Load Case) input record** and how the chosen load case (and related selections) affects which **stored results** are presented in the output. The document notes that some items are not yet used: **T, MAT, REF, NMAT, CS**. It further clarifies the key semantic rule: *the input of a load case (or design load case) determines the reference for all results stored relative to that load case*. In particular, the table’s fields control selection of beam/stress representations that originate from other program modules and how they map to the current load case output.

### Columns
- **Item**: Field name within the LC record (e.g., ENO, X, CUTP, SECT, TITL, HİST).
- **Description**: Meaning and selection rules, including defaults and equivalence relations.
- **Unit**: Unit or placeholder for expected type (often `- /LIT` to indicate a library/integer-like identifier).
- **Default**: Default value or “FIRS” (first/initial/default reference), or `NONE`, or database-derived default.

### Field semantics
1. **ENO**  
   - Meaning: **Beam number for stresses from program AQB**.  
   - Rule: “The input (except for NAME/FIND) is equivalently to NO.” This means ENO acts as an alias/alternative addressing mechanism for the beam identifier used in the context of LC-related stress representation.  
   - Default: **FIRS** (selects the first valid entry/reference when not specified).

2. **X**  
   - Meaning: **Beam abscissa** for **area stresses** from program AQB.  
   - Rule: Same equivalence note: input (except for NAME/FIND) is equivalent to **NO**.  
   - Default: **FIRS**.

3. **CUTP**  
   - Meaning: **Cut position** selector for left/right interpretation along the considered element/section.  
   - Enumerated options:
     - **LEFT**: “from left side”
     - **RIGHT**: “from right side”
     - **NONE**: no explicit position (default behavior)
   - Unit: `- /LIT`
   - Default: **NONE**.

4. **SECT**  
   - Meaning: **Cross section number** for representations on **cross sections** (linked to record **QUER**).  
   - Rule: Input (except for NAME/FIND) is equivalent to **NO**, indicating a consistent addressing convention across the system.  
   - Default: **FIRS**.

5. **TITL**  
   - Meaning: **Title of the load case** shown in the legend (default is as stored in the database; indicated as “default as in the database”).  
   - Unit: literal marker `LIT` related to identifier/text handling.  
   - Default: `*` meaning “use database/default”.

6. **HIST**  
   - Meaning: **History case selection** (history case selection controls which historical state is referenced).  
   - Rule: Input (except for NAME/FIND) is equivalently to **NO** (same aliasing/addressing convention).  
   - Default: **FIRS**.

### Context notes relevant to the LC record
- Reinforcement and design stresses from **BEMESS**, plus beam stresses from **AQB**, are represented when a **design load case** is provided. All other load-case-wise stored results are addressed by **NO**.
- Results (e.g., stresses) are stored in **beam sections**; with the input of **ENO and X**, the beam section for the **current load case** is selected.
- The record supports requesting **multiple load/design/history cases or multiple cross sections in one list** (REPR DLST), by writing numbers in one row or using a generation instruction (e.g., “LC NO 1,2,3,4,5” or “LC NO (1 5 1)” for a range-like expansion).

The table describes configuration items for controlling how result data are printed in tabular form in SOfiSTiK result table/list outputs. It is organized as a set of records where each row (or block) defines one input item, its meaning, the expected value unit/type, and the default behavior.

**Table fields / columns**
- **DBO Item** (left): The keyword used in input decks (e.g., `UNIT`, `ND`, `POSI`/`POS`, `WIDT`, `SORT`, `REPE`, `FORM`, `BMIN`, `BMAX`, `TITL`).
- **Item / Description** (middle): Human-readable explanation of what the item controls.
- **Description (second “Description” column)**: Further clarifications, option lists, or rules.
- **Unit** (right column): Typically `LIT`, meaning a literal/value string is expected; some items show `-` where no unit applies.
- **Default** (right-most): Default setting (often `*`, meaning “use global default for all columns”, or `ON`/`NO` where explicit defaults exist).

**Key configuration items**
1. **NAME**: Identifies the name of a result to be printed. The text also notes that `NAME` and `UNIT` must correspond to valid entries defined in the database description `CDBASE.CHM`.
2. **OPTI**: Controls column visibility.
   - `OFF`: value is not visible
   - `ON` (default): value is visible
3. **UNIT**: Sets the dimension/unit for the output column (e.g., a dimension definition rather than a free string). Default is `-` (no special default shown).
4. **ND**: Number of decimal places.
   - Defaults to `-` (not explicitly specified in the snippet)
   - Supports integer counts `1-9`
   - Supports E-formats `E1-E9` for scientific notation with a corresponding number of decimals.
   - Context note: decimal precision for node-supported force `PZ` can be changed using `DBO 'n_disp.pz' ND 4`.
   - Also used for graphical results, meaning the setting affects both tabular and plot outputs.
5. **POS**: Defines the column position in a table/list layout. Default `*` indicates column-wise override using the global default.
6. **WIDT**: Column width measured as number of digits. Default `*` similarly indicates it can inherit/override a global default.
   - Context note: changing default width of *all* columns can be done with `DBO '*' WIDT 15`.
7. **SORT**: Sorting behavior of the column.
   - `NO` (default): unsorted
   - `ASCE`: ascending order
   - `DESC`: descending order
8. **REPE**: Repetition behavior of recurring values in the table.
   - `NO` / `YES` options described
   - Default `*` means it uses the global column/default behavior.
   - Context note: by default, the numbers like load case/design case/cross section are printed only once per page if unchanged; `REPE` can change this. Additionally, floating-point values are always written per row.
9. **FORM**: Enables conditional formatting for table cells (not available in the “Result Browser”).
   - `NO` (default): no formatting
   - Otherwise accepts a literal combining a **format letter** and/or **rule letter**.
   - **Format letters (C/R/W)** describe how coloring/behavior is applied relative to the zero/middle and direction (e.g., left/right or from middle).
   - **Rule letters (A/m/G/S/B/O/E)** specify selection criteria such as all values, greater than `BMAX`, less than `BMIN`, between, outside, or equal.
   - Context note: values for `BMIN`/`BMAX` must be given in **m, kN, sec** units according to the relevant result dimensions.
10. **BMIN** / **BMAX**: Minimum and maximum thresholds used by conditional formatting. Default `*` indicates inheriting global settings.
11. **TITL**: Allows changing the displayed column title. Default `-` (no explicit default change).

**Row ordering and layout behavior (global context)**
Beyond the per-item definitions, the accompanying text specifies output ordering logic:
- Default row order is: **load case/design case/cross section number**, then **localization values** (e.g., beam number and abscissa), and finally **result values**.
- With `POSI` and a row-position input, this ordering can be changed.
- For readability, recurring non-floating identifiers may be printed once per page unless `REPE` is used to force repetition.
- Values to the right of any floating-point column are always written for each row, independent of `REPE`.

Overall, this table is a schema-like specification of input keywords that control formatting, numeric precision, sorting, column layout, conditional coloring thresholds, and header text for generated results tables/lists.

The table describes a configuration record named **DIAG**, which controls **properties of diagrams**—specifically how result graphs are plotted and how supplementary visual elements (axes behavior, legend, load-case labels, etc.) appear. It is structured with four columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. Each “Item” represents a configurable parameter; the “Description” explains what it controls and, where applicable, enumerates allowed values. The “Unit” column is labeled **LIT** for all parameters, indicating these fields are literal/enumerated inputs rather than measured quantities. The “Default” column specifies the standard behavior when the parameter is not explicitly set.

Key parameters:

1. **X**  
   - **Meaning:** Specifies the **Result X axis**.  
   - **Type/Unit:** LIT (selection of a result variable).  
   - **Default:** “-” (no default value defined; must be provided by the user/config).

2. **Y**  
   - **Meaning:** Specifies the **Result Y axis**.  
   - **Type/Unit:** LIT.  
   - **Default:** “-” (no default).

3. **GDEF**  
   - **Meaning:** Defines the **graph definition column** (i.e., which column/field defines how the graph is constructed from the underlying data).  
   - **Type/Unit:** LIT.  
   - **Default:** “-”.

4. **LCTP** (Labels of LC axis)  
   - **Meaning:** Controls the labeling scheme for the LC (load case) axis.  
   - **Default:** **NR**.  
   - **Allowed values (enumerated):**  
     - **NR**: Load case number  
     - **NAME**: Load case description  
     - **NRNM**: Number + name (combined label)

5. **YUP** (Invert Y axis)  
   - **Meaning:** Determines whether the **Y axis is inverted**.  
   - **Default:** **NO**.  
   - **Allowed values:**  
     - **NO**: Do not invert  
     - **YES**: Invert

6. **LEGE** (Legend)  
   - **Meaning:** Controls whether a **legend** is displayed and its style.  
   - **Default:** **DIAG**.  
   - **Allowed values:**  
     - **NO**: No legend  
     - **DIAG**: “Below diagram” legend placement

7. **SPPL** (Show support placements on axis)  
   - **Meaning:** Toggles visualization of **support placements** along the axis.  
   - **Default:** **NO**.  
   - **Allowed values:**  
     - **NO**: Do not show  
     - **YES**: Show

8. **AXFU** (Visualize full length of axis)  
   - **Meaning:** Controls whether the axis is rendered at **full length**.  
   - **Default:** **NO**.  
   - **Allowed values:**  
     - **NO**: Do not visualize full length  
     - **YES**: Visualize full length

Overall, this DIAG record centralizes diagram/plot presentation settings: it binds result axes (**X**, **Y**) to data fields, selects how graph data is defined (**GDEF**), and configures display options for load-case labeling (**LCTP**), axis direction (**YUP**), legend placement (**LEGE**), additional structural markers (**SPPL**), and axis extent (**AXFU**).

The table describes a configuration block for generating/parameterizing graphical outputs (diagrams) related to structural results plotted against independent variables such as loadcase number. It appears to define standard “items” (keywords/fields) that control the behavior of a diagram record that can include multiple data series (“graphs”) via value selectors (e.g., node IDs or beam positions).

**Column meanings**
- **Item**: The keyword/field name used in the input.
- **Description**: Human-readable meaning of the field.
- **Unit**: Unit type expected for that field (or the literal unit category).
- **Default**: Default value when the field is not provided.

**Rows / fields**
1. **DESC**
   - **Description**: Free-text label/description.
   - **Unit**: `LIT` (literal/text).
   - **Default**: `-` (no default specified).

2. **VAL1, VAL2, VAL3, VAL4, VAL5**
   - **Description**: Generic parameter placeholders (“Value 1” … “Value 5”).
   - **Unit**: `!` for **VAL1**, and `-` (unspecified) for VAL2–VAL5.
   - **Default**: `-` for all, indicating these values are optional or context-dependent rather than having fixed defaults.
   - **Interpretation in context**: In the surrounding DGRA examples, these VAL fields are used to select which entities (nodes/beams) the graph series should be created for. For instance:
     - For node-based displacement plots, the record uses **DGRA VAL1 1020** and **DGRA VAL1 1021** to generate two graphs for nodes 1020 and 1021.
     - For beam force plots, the record uses pairs like **VAL1 1 VAL2 0** and **VAL1 1 VAL2 2.700000** to define value pairs (beam number and position along the beam), producing multiple graphs for the specified locations.

3. **AXFL**
   - **Description**: “Apply set graph filling color to” and then enumerates:
     - **X**: X-axis
     - **Y**: Y-axis
   - **Unit**: `LIT`
   - **Default**: `X`
   - **Interpretation**: Controls visual formatting—specifically whether a predefined “graph filling color” setting is applied to the X axis or Y axis. If not specified, it applies to the X axis.

**Overall role**
This table acts as documentation for the diagram/DGRA-like record syntax: it specifies how to label the diagram (DESC), how to pass multiple entity-selection parameters (VAL1–VAL5) that determine which result curves are generated, and how to control axis styling (AXFL) for the resulting graphs.

The table defines configurable properties for “diagram axes,” controlled through a DIAX record (“Properties of diagram axes can be modified using this record”). It lists each configurable item, a brief description of its meaning, the unit/type associated with the setting, and a default value.

**Structure/columns**
- **Item**: The name/key of the property to configure (e.g., AXIS, MODE, TICK, LABL).
- **Description**: Explains what the setting controls and provides sub-options.
- **Unit**: Indicates the expected data format or measurement unit. In this table, the unit column generally uses **LIT**, suggesting a literal/enumerated value or a code-type input rather than a physical measurement.
- **Default**: The default behavior if the property is not explicitly set.

**Rows / properties**
1. **AXIS**
   - **Description**: Selects which axis the modification applies to.
     - **X** = X axis  
     - **Y** = Y axis
   - **Unit**: **LIT**
   - **Default**: **X**  
   - **Implication**: If AXIS is not set, changes apply to the X axis by default.

2. **MODE**
   - **Description**: Controls how ticks and labels are generated/rendered.
     - **AUTO** = automatic tick/label placement  
     - **USER** = user-defined tick/label placement
   - **Unit**: **LIT**
   - **Default**: **AUTO**  
   - **Implication**: By default, the system determines tick intervals and labels automatically. Switching to **USER** enables manual interval control using TICK and LABL.

3. **TICK**
   - **Description**: Specifies the spacing **between tick marks** when **MODE = USER**.
   - **Unit**: **—** (shown as a dash; the table does not specify a physical unit, implying it is an interval/count value relevant to the diagram’s axis scale)
   - **Default**: **!** (an exclamation-mark placeholder indicating no valid default/required value is defined unless MODE=USER).  
   - **Implication**: TICK is effectively meaningful only when MODE is set to USER.

4. **LABL**
   - **Description**: Specifies the spacing **between labeled tick marks** when **MODE = USER** (i.e., how frequently labels appear along the axis).
   - **Unit**: **—**
   - **Default**: **!**  
   - **Implication**: Like TICK, LABL is relevant only under USER mode, and the table suggests no applicable default is provided.

**Overall behavior summary**
This DIAX configuration record primarily selects the target axis (X or Y), chooses whether ticks/labels are automatic or user-controlled, and—when user-controlled—sets two intervals: **TICK** for tick spacing and **LABL** for label spacing.

The provided table describes the **“3.16 DIAP – Additional diagram properties”** record (labeled **DIAP**). It is structured as a small specification table with four columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. The intent of this record is to define extra properties that apply to diagrams, specifically focusing on how an additional line within a diagram is aligned and how that line’s value and description are stored.

### Table structure
- **Item**: A short field identifier used in the record.
- **Description**: A human-readable explanation of what the field controls.
- **Unit**: The expected unit/type for the field.
- **Default**: The default value used when the field is not explicitly provided.

### Fields described in this table
1. **ALIG — Alignment of the line**
   - **Purpose**: Controls how the additional line is positioned/oriented in the diagram.
   - **Sub-options**:
     - **HOR** = horizontal alignment
     - **VER** = vertical alignment
   - **Unit**: **LIT** (indicates the field value is a coded literal / enumerated literal in the associated specification system).
   - **Default**: **HOR**  
   *Meaning*: If no alignment is specified, the additional line aligns horizontally by default.

2. **VAL — Value**
   - **Purpose**: Provides a numeric or parameterized value associated with the property/line (e.g., the magnitude or coordinate-like setting depending on the broader diagram definition context).
   - **Unit**: **—** (not specified as having a particular unit in this table; the value is treated as a generic “Value”).
   - **Default**: **!**  
   *Meaning*: The default is a special marker “!” rather than a normal numeric default, implying a required or flagged value behavior within the source specification.

3. **DESC — Description**
   - **Purpose**: A textual description tied to the property/line (often used for labeling, annotations, or metadata for diagram interpretation).
   - **Unit**: **LIT** (again indicating a literal/text-based field).
   - **Default**: **-**  
   *Meaning*: If not supplied, the description defaults to a dash placeholder.

### Key takeaways for RAG indexing
- This table defines **three configurable attributes** under **DIAP**: **ALIG** (horizontal/vertical alignment), **VAL** (associated value), and **DESC** (free text description).
- **ALIG** defaults to **HOR**, making horizontal alignment the assumed behavior.
- **VAL** and **DESC** use special placeholder defaults (**!** and **-** respectively), suggesting sentinel behavior or optional/required handling per the larger specification.
- The table is primarily about **additional diagram line properties**, particularly **alignment**, plus storage of a **value** and a **description**.

The input table documents options for labeling or selecting **extreme value results** within the DLAB result processing workflow (in the context of records such as **FLT – filtering results** and **FILT – extreme value selection**). It contains three columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. The highlighted items are **MODE** and **THRH**, both of which control what subset of values is produced/annotated and how extremes are evaluated.

### MODE
- **Item:** `MODE`  
- **Description:** Defines the “values to be labeled,” i.e., which result values (or groups of values) are treated as candidates for extreme-value labeling/selection.
- **Unit:** `LIT` (labeling/selection mode indicator; not a physical unit).
- **Default:** `NONE`.

Supported `MODE` values listed in the table:
- `NONE`: No special labeling.
- `GLEX`: Global extreme values (extremes across the whole dataset).
- `EXTR`: Extreme values (general extreme-value mode).
- `ALL`: All values.
- `E2ND`: Each second value.
- `E3RD`: Each third value.
- `E4TH`: Each fourth value.
- `E5TH`: Each fifth value.

These options allow switching between “true extreme picking” (e.g., global/extreme) and “periodic sampling” (e.g., every 2nd/3rd/4th/5th value), or disabling labeling.

### THRH
- **Item:** `THRH`  
- **Description:** A threshold parameter used **between extreme values to be labeled**, specifically **when `MODE = EXTR`**. It controls how close successive extreme selections can be (i.e., it filters/limits which extremes are labeled).
- **Unit:** `–` (dimensionless or not applicable).
- **Default:** `0`.

### Relationship to FLT / FILT context
While this table only defines `MODE` and `THRH`, it fits into the broader mechanism described for **FILT – Extreme Value Selection**, where:
- `NAME` identifies valid SOFiSTiK database result fields (must match `CDBASE.CHM`),
- `TYPE` adds/removes filters for selected results,
- `EXRF` defines a reference column used to compute min/max per reference value (e.g., per load case),
- and `MODE` / `THRH` further determine how extremes are labeled/filtered when selecting results (notably in `MODE = EXTR`).

The table describes the fields of the **FLT** record, which is used in DLAB **3.18 FLT – Filtering results** to restrict which result rows are displayed. In the overall filtering mechanism, filters are grouped into **filter sets** and then combined so that conditions within one set are combined with **AND**, while different sets are combined with **OR**.

### Columns
- **Item**: The field name in the FLT record.
- **Description**: What the field controls.
- **Unit**: Unit type for the field (here mostly textual/meta fields; no physical units are applicable).
- **Default**: Default value behavior for the field.

### Fields and semantics
1. **ID**
   - **Meaning**: Identifier of a filter set (**must be > 0**).
   - **How it’s used**: Rows with the **same ID** are treated as belonging to the same filter set, therefore their conditions are joined using **AND**. Different IDs create separate filter sets, which are then combined using **OR**.

2. **NAME**
   - **Meaning**: The “result item” (column/quantity) that the filter will be applied to.
   - **Constraint**: The value must correspond to a valid item name from the SOFiSTiK database description **CDBASE.CHM** (i.e., the referenced result quantity must exist and be recognized by SOFiSTiK).

3. **RULE**
   - **Meaning**: The filter expression that determines which rows are accepted.
   - **Typical usage**: It compares the chosen result item (**NAME**) against some criterion (e.g., thresholds or explicit values). The rule content is a **filter expression string**; the documentation context notes allowed conditions are expressed as such comparisons.

4. **ACT**
   - **Meaning**: Controls whether the filter row is visible/active in the configuration output.
   - **Values**:
     - **YES**: Show filter
     - **NO**: Hide filter
   - **Default**: **YES**, meaning filters are shown unless explicitly hidden.

### Overall behavior (from the surrounding context)
FLT entries define multiple conditional constraints over result data. By careful assignment of **ID** values, users can build complex logical logic:
- **Same ID → AND** (all conditions must hold).
- **Different IDs → OR** (any condition set may match).
In addition, filters may reference nodal or displacement-related quantities (e.g., `n_disp.nr`, `n_disp.ux`) and apply thresholds or exact matches using **RULE**.

This table fragment documents **filtering and extreme value selection** features used in the DLAB module (SOFiSTiK-related post-processing). It contains two main sections—**FLT (Filtering results)** and **FILT (Extreme Value Selection)**—plus a compact **syntax reference** table that defines how textual conditions are interpreted for rule-based filtering.

## 3.18 FLT – Filtering results
**Purpose:** Filter a set of result rows using one or more filter records.

**Core mechanics:**
- Filters are applied through this record type: **FLT**.
- A **filter set** is formed by rows that share the same **ID**.
- Within a filter set, all conditions are combined with **logical AND**:  
  *“All filters of a filter set will be AND joined.”*
- Multiple filter sets are combined with **logical OR**:
  *“Several filter sets will be joined using OR.”*
- The assignment of a filter row to a filter set is determined by its **ID** value.

**Valid item names:**
- The **NAME** field must match valid entries from the SOFiSTiK database description **CDBASE.CHM** (i.e., only recognized result-column identifiers may be used).

**Condition specification:**
- Each row defines a condition using **RULE**.
- **OPTI** controls whether the filter is active (i.e., it can enable/disable the condition).
- The examples illustrate two common boolean patterns:
  - **AND within one ID:**  
    Same ID, different conditions (e.g., node number > 1009 AND displacement > 0.1).
  - **OR across IDs:**  
    Different IDs for alternative criteria (e.g., node number equals 1010 OR equals 1020).

## 3.19 FILT – Extreme Value Selection
**Purpose:** Select and summarize **extreme values** (min/max) after filtering, with additional options beyond FLT.

**Relations to FLT:**
- Extreme value selection is done via **FILT**.
- “For more filter options see FLT,” implying FILT complements FLT.

**Key parameters:**
- **NAME:** Specifies which database column (again, must be valid per CDBASE.CHM) the extreme evaluation targets.
- **TYPE:** Determines whether filters are added or removed for the selected result (EXTREME selection is influenced by this).
- **EXRF:** Defines the **reference column(s)** used to compute extremes per group. Multiple columns may be provided as a **comma-separated list**.
- If **EXRF is not specified**, extremes are computed across **all available rows**.

**Example behavior described in text:**
- An input like:
  `FILT NAME "n_disp.ux" TYPE EX EXRF "n_disp.__kwl" NODE TYPE UX REPR DLST`
  produces a table with **min and max nodal displacement** for each **load case**, where the grouping reference is provided by **EXRF**.

## Syntax reference (condition/RULE semantics)
The bottom portion is a general-purpose **RULE syntax** table, defining how a RULE string is interpreted:
- `!` → negates the following expression.
- `x` or `=x` → values equal X.
- `>x`, `>=x`, `<x`, `<=x` → numeric comparisons.
- Ranges:
  - `[FROM;TO]` inclusive bounds
  - `[FROM;TO[` include FROM, exclude TO
  - `]FROM;TO]` exclude FROM, include TO
  - `]FROM;TO[` exclude both
- `(FROM;TO;INCR)` → range with increment step INCR.
- `*` → wildcard for any characters (e.g., `max*` matches strings starting with “max”).
- `?` → wildcard for exactly one character (e.g., `a?c` matches abac-like patterns but not “abc” with mismatched lengths).

Overall, the table defines both the **data selection logic** (AND/OR grouping, rule conditions, activation via OPTI) and the **extreme-value computation workflow** (FILT with grouping via EXRF).

The table describes the configuration fields for **FILT – Extreme Value Selection**, a SOFiSTiK DLAB record used to extract extreme results from a result dataset. It works together with the more general **FLT – Filtering results** mechanism, but focuses specifically on selecting minima/maxima rather than applying threshold filters to individual rows.

### Columns
- **Item**: the parameter name used in the record.
- **Description**: what the parameter controls.
- **Unit**: unit metadata (for these fields mostly marked as text identifiers like **LIT** or “-”).
- **Default**: the default value if the field is not provided.

### Parameters
1. **NAME (Name of the result)**  
   - Specifies the result quantity to evaluate (e.g., a nodal displacement component).  
   - The value must be a valid item name from the SOFiSTiK database, particularly consistent with the database description referenced in the context (e.g., `CDBASE.CHM`).  
   - **Default**: `!` (required/mandatory; not given as a fixed default).

2. **TYPE (Kind of filtering)**  
   - Controls whether filtering is performed and the mode of interpretation:
     - **NO**: *No filtering*; shows all values.
     - **EX**: *Extreme values*; enables extreme-value selection behavior.
   - **Default**: `!` (effectively mandatory in the context of enabling the record’s behavior).

3. **EXRF (Reference column used for extreme values)**  
   - Defines the **grouping/reference column** used to compute extremes separately for each reference value.  
   - When provided, the system calculates extreme values of `NAME` for each distinct value in the reference column (e.g., per load case or per another categorizing attribute).  
   - **Default**: `-` (no reference column provided).

4. **EXTP (Type of extreme value filter)**  
   - Determines which extreme(s) are returned:
     - **MIN**: only minimum values
     - **MAX**: only maximum values
     - **MIMA**: minimum and maximum values
   - **Default**: `MIMA` (both min and max are produced if not overridden).

### Overall behavior
- With `TYPE=EX`, the record selects extreme values of the quantity specified by **NAME**.
- If **EXRF** is set (possibly to multiple columns via comma-separated list in the wider context), extreme selection is performed **per reference group**; otherwise, extremes are taken over **all available rows**.
- **EXTP** controls whether minima, maxima, or both are output.

The input table documents configuration parameters that control how an “additional information” block (referred to as **TINF**) is displayed at the end of a table. It provides a structured way to define *which types* of extra summary values are shown and *how/where* they appear, differentiating between interactive use and report generation.

## Table structure (columns)
- **Item**: Identifier for each configuration parameter (e.g., TYPE, MEDI, OPTI).
- **Description**: Meaning of the parameter and its allowed values.
- **Unit**: Data type or expected input kind (e.g., **LIT**, **INT**, or “-” when not applicable).
- **Default**: Default setting(s) for that parameter when no explicit TINF record is provided. Some entries show “-”, indicating no single default applies or the field is conceptual rather than value-driven.

## Row-by-row content

### 1) **TYPE** (Unit: LIT; Default: “-”)
Defines *what kind* of summary information is produced and displayed:
- **ALL**: show **all** types of summary information
- **MIN**: show the **minimum**
- **MAX**: show the **maximum**
- **TOTA**: show the **total**

This parameter represents the category of statistics/aggregates appended after the table.

### 2) **MEDI** (Unit: LIT; Default: **INT**)
Specifies the **affected output target**—i.e., which interface or output mode the TINF behavior applies to:
- **INT**: **User Interface (Result Viewer)**
- **REP**: **Report**

The default is **INT**, meaning the default behavior targets the interactive result viewer unless changed.

### 3) **OPTI** (Unit: LIT; Default: “-”)
Controls **visibility** of the additional information:
- **NO**: not visible
- **YES**: visible

This determines whether the selected additional info is actually displayed.

## Additional context: overall defaults for TINF
When no TINF record is specified, the system uses different defaults depending on context:
- **Defaults (Interactive / Result Viewer):**
  - **MIN NO**
  - **MAX NO**
  - **TOTA NO**

- **Defaults (Reports):**
  - **MIN YES**
  - **MAX YES**
  - **TOTA NO**
  → meaning minimum and maximum are shown in reports, but total is not.

In summary, the table defines three related controls—**what** summary stats (TYPE), **where** they apply (MEDI), and **whether** they are visible (OPTI)—with context-dependent defaults for interactive viewing versus report output.

     - `DIRE`: observer looks **from infinite distance behind** the origin (parallel projection), so (X, Y, Z) indicates a point behind the origin relative to the observer.
     - `STAN`: observer looks **from infinite distance in front of** the origin.

   A third mode is also referenced in the additional context:
   - `ANGL`: (X, Y, Z) represent **angles** (x, y, z) of the corresponding axes toward the horizontal direction. The table excerpt itself does not list all values of `TYPE`, but the context clarifies the supported interpretation.

     - `NEGX`: negative x axis points downward
     - `NEGY`: negative y axis points downward

Together, these fields determine how a 3D coordinate system is projected onto a 2D drawing: `TYPE` selects whether direction is defined via vector components or via angles; `X/Y/Z` encode that definition; `AXIS` sets which coordinate axis points downward for the observer; and `ROTA` applies an extra clockwise roll of the final view.
